title: _get_user_slug falls back to os.getlogin(), which raises OSError when stdin is not a TTY (servers/containers)
description: When `git config user.name` is unset/empty, `_get_user_slug` falls back to `os.getlogin()`. `os.getlogin()` reads the controlling terminal and raises `OSError: [Errno 25] Inappropriate ioctl for device` (or similar) in any environment without a controlling TTY — daemonized servers, many Docker containers, systemd services, and some CI runners. Because `_get_user_slug` is called inside `get_status`, `create_branch`, and `list_branches`, an unconfigured git identity in such an environment turns into an UNCAUGHT OSError that escapes the GitError funnel and becomes a generic HTTP 500, rather than a clean, branch-able username. The codebase already has the correct, robust idiom for exactly this in src/haute/deploy/_utils.py:get_user(), which uses `getpass.getuser()` wrapped in `except (KeyError, OSError)`. getpass.getuser() consults LOGNAME/USER/LNAME/USERNAME env vars before falling back, so it works headless; os.getlogin() does not. This helper is inconsistent with that established pattern and is the fragile choice.
evidence: Line 202: `return _slugify(os.getlogin())`. Contrast src/haute/deploy/_utils.py:15-20 `get_user()` -> `try: return getpass.getuser() except (KeyError, OSError): return 'unknown'`, whose tests (tests/test_deploy_utils.py:96-104) explicitly cover `OSError('no tty')` and `KeyError('no user')`. _git has no analogous guard and uses the more failure-prone os.getlogin().
